sections.h2: Where Kalkaska County deeds are recorded
sections.html:
Deeds are filed with the Register of Deeds in the Administration Building, 605 N. Birch Street, village of Kalkaska, MI 49646. The phone is 231-258-3315. Administration hours on weekdays are 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., and legal holidays are observed. The counter also takes passport applications, by appointment only.

Cabins, lake lots and acreage anywhere in the county all record here, at the one office for the entire county. The village of Kalkaska is the county's only village and its seat.

Indexing and recording a deed, mortgage, lis pendens, affidavit or any other instrument costs $30 for the whole paper. There has been no per page charge since October 1, 2016. A document that discharges or assigns mortgages adds $3 for each extra instrument number. See MCL 600.2567.

Warranty covenant deeds, land contracts and land contract assignments need a county treasurer tax certificate first. The price is $5.00 per instrument for as many as five descriptions, then 20 cents for each further description. That adds up when a sale spans several parcels.

  • Cards work through an online county payment page, using a paycode posted on the register of deeds page.
  • Plat books are sold at the counter for cash or check.
  • A free property fraud alert notifies you of any document recorded with your name in it.

A deed worth $100 or more triggers both taxes, and the grantor pays them. The county share is 55 cents per $500 under MCL 207.504, and the state share is $3.75 per $500. The county website has a chart for looking up any price.

Put the property value on the deed, or file a valuation affidavit. The affidavit costs nothing but must be noted on the deed. An exemption claimed under MCL 207.505 for the county or MCL 207.526 for the state has to be written on the deed too.

sections.h2: Deeds that owe no transfer tax
sections.html:
Exemptions come from the two transfer tax acts, and the county posts both lists on its recording fees page. Both exempt security instruments, leases and deeds from a government grantor, along with confirmation deeds, such as a quitclaim that repairs a flaw in a title the grantee already holds.

Family transfers split. Only the state act exempts a deed from a parent to a child, stepchild, grandchild or step-grandchild. The same statute also exempts foreclosure deeds and deeds in lieu, though a later resale by the foreclosing party is taxed.

Whichever exemption applies, write it on the deed. If tax was paid on a deed that qualified, the state act lets the seller request a refund from the state treasury.

Most document types can be e-recorded. Judgments, court orders, plats, surveys and other certified papers cannot. The partner vendors are ePN, CSC, Indecomm and Simplifile. Simplifile alone handles warranty deeds, land contracts and other treasurer certified papers.

Title professionals sign up for Laredo, the county's records search program, by sending the register of deeds a subscription agreement. Individual owners can use the fraud alert and the front counter.

A one time seller is usually best served when the title company or closing attorney e-records. To carry a paper deed instead, read the layout list below first, because a returned deed can delay closing.

MCL 565.201 binds this office like any other, and an instrument missing an item cannot be accepted. Homemade deeds tend to fail on these points:

  • 2.5 inches of open space atop page one, and half inch margins around the rest.
  • Dark print, 10 point type, on white paper no lighter than 20 pound.
  • A single phrase on the first printed line naming what is being recorded.
  • Names printed beneath every signature, and the notary's name beside the notary signature.
  • The grantee's address, plus the drafter's name and business address.
  • An attached English translation when part of the text is in another language.

The statute adds that anything already recorded is conclusively presumed to comply, so a deed that clears the counter stays on record even if a small slip went unnoticed.

sections.h2: Filing a paper deed yourself, step by step
sections.html:
Start by deciding which deed you hold. A warranty covenant deed or land contract needs the treasurer's certificate first, so visit the county treasurer before the register of deeds. Next, check your document against the layout list above, including the blank strip on page one and the printed names under every signature.

Then take the original to 605 N. Birch Street with the $30 recording fee and the transfer tax. State the value on the deed or attach the valuation affidavit, and write any exemption on the deed. Card payers use the county payment page and the posted paycode.

Afterward, sign up for the free fraud alert with your name so you hear about any document recorded against your property. It costs nothing and works for individuals and businesses. If a deed ever appears that you did not sign, call 231-258-3315 right away and ask what steps the office can take.

This is a small market where nearly everyone owns. The county has 18,693 residents in 11,820 housing units, a gain of 4.2 percent over the April 2020 base. Owners live in 88.2 percent of occupied homes. The middle home value is $188,900, and median rent is $853 a month.

About 24.6 percent of residents are past 65, and density is only 32 people per square mile. Buyers sometimes arrive from neighboring counties such as Antrim, Otsego, Crawford, Roscommon, Missaukee, Wexford and Grand Traverse, so ask the closing agent early where each party will sign.

sections.h2: What to line up before closing
sections.html:
Pick up the certificate and any tax payoff figure from the county treasurer, and let the register of deeds look over your paperwork. Confirm the treasurer's hours and number before you head over, since schedules change.

Agree with your title company on who pays each of these, so nothing is paid twice:

  • The $30 deed filing charge.
  • The treasurer's certificate, $5 for a short parcel list.
  • Both transfer taxes, which land on the seller.

If the sale includes several parcels, count the descriptions early, because each one past five adds 20 cents to the certificate.

If you sell for cash, the same recording steps apply, but there is no lender's list of title requirements to satisfy. Ask the buyer's closing agent which of the items above they will handle.

faqs.q: What does the Register of Deeds charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: Thirty dollars covers a whole document of any length. A paper assigning or discharging several mortgages adds $3 for each extra instrument number.

faqs.q: Does a Kalkaska County deed need a tax certificate?
faqs.a: It does when the deed has a warranty covenant, and for land contracts and their assignments. The treasurer charges $5.00 an instrument for up to five descriptions.

faqs.q: Who pays Kalkaska County transfer tax?
faqs.a: The seller does. Recording triggers 55 cents for the county and $3.75 for the state per $500 of price, unless an exemption stated on the deed applies.

Yes. The register of deeds page links a county card payment service and gives a paycode to use. Treat the treasurer's tax certificate fee as a separate payment and ask that office how it takes payment.

faqs.q: What number do I call at the Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Dial 231-258-3315. The counter is at 605 N. Birch Street in Kalkaska and keeps weekday administration hours.
